description: TRACK a product: pin an Amazon ASIN into our hot lane so its all-offers page is re-read every hour or every 2, 4, 12 or 24 hours, for as long as the plan is active (or a ttl_days you set), with e-mail and webhook alerts on the thresholds you give; every read lands in the product's history as a sub-daily buy-box point (price, buy-box seller, fulfillment, offer count - buybox_price_points_hot on the product tool). read=product_page (2026-10-29) reads the product page and its offers page instead, so the SALES RANK is read too: every reading lands in bsr_points_hot (and its offers page in buybox_price_points_hot); such a read draws 2 snapshots of the allowance. USE WHEN the user wants to watch a product's price, buy box, seller count or sales rank more often than our normal cadence: repricing, MAP and buy-box monitoring, a competitor's listing, a launch, a deal, a book's rank. Posting the same ASIN again renews it and changes its interval. DON'T USE to read data (product, offers): tracking only schedules the reads. COST 0 credits: what a plan sells is a daily allowance of tracked snapshots (Solo 2,500 a day = 416 products every 4 hours, Starter 6,000, Growth 18,000, Standard 40,000, Scale 170,000, Volume 710,000); when the allowance is spent the answer says so with the upgrade link, and when only a longer interval fits it is granted (granted_interval). RETURNS id, asin, country, status (active / paused / expired / stopped), interval, read, granted_interval, requested_interval, snapshots_per_day (reads_per_day too for product_page), expires_at, in_lane, last_snapshot_at, next_due_at, pending (true until the lane picks it up, within ~10 minutes), allowance (plan, snapshots_per_day, used, remaining). action=stop ends a tracking at once (by id from list_tracked, or by asin + country) and releases its allowance; the row stays listed 30 days as stopped. BULK (2026-10-14): asins (up to 10,000) with action=track / stop, and action=sync to make the active set equal to a list (dry_run first). STOCK STATES: every read is in_stock (a buy box), no_buybox (offers, no featured offer) or out_of_stock (no offers, confirmed twice); availability_change / out_of_stock / back_in_stock alert on the transitions, price alerts compare buy-box prices only. Paid plans only (the allowance belongs to a subscription). MARKETPLACES us, uk, de, ca, au, fr, it, es, jp, mx, br (no Walmart).

action.description: track (default) creates or renews the tracking(s); stop ends one or many at once; sync (2026-10-14) makes the account's active set on one marketplace EQUAL to asins: missing ones are created, active ones not listed are stopped, the rest are left as they are - dry_run first to see the counts.

alert_email.description: Optional: e-mail alerts for the notify_if thresholds - 'true' for the account's own address, or an address. One e-mail per event, at most 50 a day per tracking. 'false' detaches. Works with or without webhook_url.

asin.description: The product's 10-character Amazon ASIN (one product). Or give asins.

asins.description: Bulk (2026-10-14): up to 10,000 ASINs in one call - with action=track all get the same interval / ttl_days / alerts (results[] in input order: created / renewed / refused / invalid, the allowance consumed in input order, never all-or-nothing); with action=stop they are stopped; with action=sync they are the full list the active set becomes.

country.description: The Amazon marketplace to track the product on.

dry_run.description: With action=sync: return what would be created and stopped without writing.

id.description: With action=stop: the tracking id (from list_tracked). Or give asin + country, or ids / asins.

ids.description: With action=stop: several tracking ids at once (up to 10,000).

interval.description: How often the lane re-reads the product (see read). A shorter interval costs more of the daily allowance (1h = 24 snapshots a day, 2h = 12, 4h = 6, 12h = 2, 24h = 1; twice that with read=product_page).

notify_if.description: With webhook_url and / or alert_email: the thresholds. price_below / price_above (a buy-box price), price_change_pct (percent move of the buy-box price since the last in-stock read), buybox_seller_change (true: a different seller holds the buy box, between two in-stock reads), offer_count_below / offer_count_above (a count), availability_change (true: the stock STATE changed - in_stock, no_buybox = offers exist but Amazon shows no featured offer, out_of_stock = no offers at all, confirmed by a second read; the event carries both codes), out_of_stock (true: shorthand for a change to out_of_stock), back_in_stock (true: a change to in_stock). {} attaches the webhook and fires on nothing.

read.description: Which page each read fetches (2026-10-29): offers (default) = the all-offers page (buy box, price, every offer, stock); product_page = the product page and its offers page, so the sales rank is read too: every reading lands in the product tool's bsr_points_hot, and its offers page in buybox_price_points_hot as with offers. A product-page read draws 2 snapshots of the allowance (12h = 4 a day). Like interval, every call sets it: tracking the same ASIN again without read switches it back to offers.

ttl_days.description: Optional: stop after this many days (1-365). Omit (or 0) and the tracking runs for as long as the plan is active - a lapsed plan keeps it 7 days, then it pauses and resumes with the plan.

webhook_url.description: Optional: an https URL Logimu POSTs to when a notify_if threshold fires on a new observation (signed X-Logimu-Signature: sha256=HMAC-SHA256(secret, body); the secret is returned once in webhook_secret). An empty string detaches it.

name: track_product
